links.outcome: Reliability of LLM-as-a-judge versus physician evaluation of model outputs
links.effect: Automated judging tracks overall trends but shows bias on fine-grained individualized distinctions, highlighting need for physician involvement when ground truth is unavailable.
links.quote: We also examine the reliability of LLM-as-a-judge versus physician evaluation: automated judging tracks overall trends but shows bias on fine-grained individualized distinctions, highlighting the need for physician involvement when ground truth is unavailable and for domain-adapted judge models.

unlisted_practices: Fine-tuning lightweight LLMs to learn distinguished physicians' diagnostic-and-therapeutic expertise
Using domain-adapted judge models for LLM-as-a-judge evaluation

screen.reason: The study evaluates a framework for training lightweight clinical LLMs and empirically evaluates LLM-as-a-judge validation against expert physician evaluation.
